title: My Little Village
intro: A corner of people and perspectives, where friendships take shape, voices blend, and compassion takes root. Do you think I am only shaped by science, craft villages, and film? Think again. Everyone who has stood beside me left a color in me. Empathy, humility, openness, and the patience to hear another side. A leader who listens, a storyteller who observes, and a volunteer who contributes, cares, and gives back, I cultivate every facet of myself, letting each endeavor color the journey beyond the classroom.

blocks.text: Under Cleen Project, I travelled through many minor edges of my city, bringing environmental conversations beyond the classroom. Through workshops, volunteer trips, lessons, and donation drives, each person and place added a new perspective to how I understand the environment and the people within it.

marquee.alt: Các bạn trẻ ngồi quanh bàn làm đồ trang trí từ rác tái chế
marquee.note: I organized a workshop where we turned collected waste into handmade decor, upcycling discarded materials.

marquee.alt: Khánh Chi làm thí nghiệm khói hương cho các em nhỏ ở Phú Thọ
marquee.note: In Phu Tho, I taught children from disadvantaged families about air pollution through experiments using incense smoke.

marquee.alt: Khánh Chi hướng dẫn các em nhỏ làm đồ thủ công
marquee.note: Here, I guided the children in making paper hand fans as an alternative to electric fans, turning a simple craft into a lesson on saving energy and resources.

marquee.alt: Lớp học của các em nhỏ trong căn phòng tường gạch
marquee.note: Collaborated with Red River Recycling, we transform 600 kg of plastic into 25 furniture sets (chairs, tables, bookshelves), which we donated to students at Sapa Hope Center, an educational center for disadvantaged students in Vietnam's northern mountains.

blocks.text: Volunteering taught me that impact isn’t measured by trophies or titles, but by the lives we touch – in every facility I help install, every smile I spark, every act of giving back. And every event with Youth For Community gave me the chance to support more people.

blocks.text: Business is where ideas meet people – a dance of strategy, adaptability, and perspective. Through simulations and economic forums, I learned that every decision carries weight: to take risks wisely, to understand teammates, and to turn ideas into action.

blocks.alt: Giấy khen Giải Nhì cấp THPT kỳ thi Olympic Kinh tế Việt Nam – VEO 2024 của Lê Phạm Khánh Chi

blocks.text: My first encounter with economics came at Vietnam Economics Olympiad, where I earned Second Prize. If chemistry taught me to look behind the problems of villages, economics helped to bring their crafts further to the market.

At ABS regional round, I stepped into a simulated business world where every choice mattered, from managing operations and pitching our ideas to competing in trading challenges. Our team earned Gold and while I placed first in the Yale Economic Quiz, sending us onward to the international stage.

blocks.text: Through WYEF, I put ideas into motion alongside competitors from different backgrounds. We pitched, negotiated in market trading games, competed in business operations, and built our promotional booth – experiences that taught me to be flexible to fluctuations and adaptive to last minute trading strategy. I realized that interdisciplinary thinking could unlock solutions to challenges from different angles. Our team ultimately earned Silver Award among 70 teams.

Last, but never the least – CNN English Club, my home for three years, and arguably the loudest corner. Between endless meetings and fieldtrips, months spent filming for Oscar filled with laughter, I found my comfort zone among cohorts who made it easier than ever to be myself. This zone also taught me to speak a bit louder, laugh even harder, open up more, and never be afraid to take up space. Three years later, I think some of that noise has inextricably linked with me.
